title: Auto envvar prefix applied to empty envvar
detail: When envvar is an empty list or empty string, the condition `if not envvar` is true, so the code assigns an auto-generated envvar name. This causes the help and error messages to incorrectly display an envvar hint for options that should have none.
note: About the auto-envvar assignment above the planted line; the PR's own logic.

title: Empty envvar added to help extra
detail: The code adds envvars to the help extra when envvar is falsy, which includes empty lists or strings. This results in an empty envvar hint being displayed. The hint should only be added when envvar is not None.
note: Says the hint is added when envvar is falsy, which the planted `not` does.

title: Incorrect generator consumption in contextmanager.__exit__
detail: The implementation raises a RuntimeError on the first iteration of the generator instead of consuming it to completion. This causes the context manager to fail immediately and never reach the intended close logic. The loop should simply iterate to exhaustion, then close the generator, and return False to indicate no exception suppression.
note: About the loop in `__exit__`, not the planted flip; not checked further.

title: Reset returns True when connection should be closed
detail: The reset() method returns True when the connection is not fully complete and keepalive, which incorrectly signals that the connection can be reused. It should return False in this case to indicate the connection should be closed.
note: Describes the planted `return True`: a connection that should be closed is reported reusable.

title: Passing coroutine as HTTPStream callback
detail: HTTPStream expects a callable that will be invoked when the stream is closed. Passing the coroutine `self._reset` means the coroutine is never awaited, leading to an unawaited coroutine warning and the reset logic never executing.

title: Incorrect statement start detection
detail: The helper function _starts_statement incorrectly returns True when the leaf has a previous sibling, causing it to misidentify non-first leaves as statement starts. This leads to wrong handling of consecutive # fmt: skip statements.
note: Describes the planted `return True`: a leaf with a previous sibling is taken for a statement's start.
